President Bola Tinubu has congratulated former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar on his 80th birthday, recalling his support for the former vice-president’s 2007 presidential aspiration under the defunct Action Congress.
Mr Tinubu, in a birthday message issued on Wednesday, 25 November, which he personally signed, commended Atiku’s contributions to Nigeria’s development and his commitment to democratic pluralism.
The president said his support for Mr Atiku’s presidential ambition in 2007 reflected his belief that democracy thrives when political actors are free to participate, offer alternative visions and contribute to national conversations on leadership and governance.
He noted that although both politicians now belong to different political parties and hold contrasting views on national issues, their shared commitment to Nigeria’s unity and democratic stability should remain paramount.
Atiku, who is the presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), served as vice-president between 1999 and 2007 under former President Olusegun Obasanjo.
Mr Tinubu also praised the former vice-president’s contributions to education, entrepreneurship and the private sector, particularly his investments in business development and job creation.
He specifically highlighted Atiku’s establishment of the American University of Nigeria, Yola, Adamawa State, describing it as a significant contribution to expanding access to quality higher education and strengthening human capital development.

The president further said his political philosophy has consistently emphasised deepening democracy, strengthening political institutions, respecting divergent opinions, and ensuring that political competition serves the broader interests of Nigerians.
He also reiterated his advocacy for politics without bitterness, saying political actors should leave room for reconciliation after disagreements with their opponents.
“As the former vice president joins the Octogenarian Club, I wish him good health, renewed strength and many more years of service to the nation and humanity,” Mr Tinubu said.
